data.name: Hiya
data.gender_notes: Hiya is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Hiya is derived from the Sanskrit word 'hīyā' which means 'sun's rays'. In Hindu mythology, the sun is considered a powerful symbol of life, energy, and vitality. The name Hiya is believed to bestow upon the child the strength, courage, and wisdom of the sun. The name Hiya carries the meaning “Sun's rays” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Hiya usually hope their child will grow to embody sun's rays and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Bringing light and warmth to those around you.
data.etymology: Hiya belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Sun's rays.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Hiya total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

historical_references.reference: Hiya was an important Hindu goddess in the Vedic pantheon, associated with fertility, motherhood, and the earth. She was considered the goddess of the earth and the embodiment of Prakriti, or material nature. Hiya was often invoked in rituals and prayers for a bountiful harvest and for the protection of children.

Hiya is also mentioned in Mahabharata, an ancient Indian epic, where she is described as the wife of the sage Vyasa and the mother of the legendary warrior Bhishma. Hiya is said to have performed severe penance to gain the boon of having a son who would rule over the battlefield and never die until he chose to do so.
